opts.name: Tiller
opts.why: More gold from everything you grow. Always pick this.

opts.name: Rancher
opts.why: Only good if you focus exclusively on animal husbandry early.

opts.name: Artisan (needs Tiller)
opts.effect: Artisan goods (wine, mayo, cheese, etc.) sell for 40% more.
opts.why: Best profession in the game. Wine/mayo income becomes astronomical.

opts.name: Agriculturist (needs Tiller)
opts.why: Decent, but Artisan's money boost far outweighs growth speed.

opts.name: Coopmaster (needs Rancher)
opts.effect: Coops befriended faster, duck mayo and rabbit's foot more frequent.
opts.why: Niche — only if you're coop-focused and skipped Tiller.

opts.name: Shepherd (needs Rancher)
opts.effect: Barns befriended faster, sheep wool grows faster.
opts.why: Good for wool/cloth farming, but still loses to Artisan overall.

opts.name: Miner
opts.why: Consistently more ore for upgrades and selling.

opts.name: Geologist
opts.effect: Chance for gem nodes to have 2 gems; Coal appears in pairs.
opts.why: Good for gem selling, but Miner's ore bonus is more universally useful.

opts.name: Blacksmith (needs Miner)
opts.why: Good mid-game, but you need bars for crafting more than selling late.

opts.name: Prospector (needs Miner)
opts.why: Coal is needed constantly for smelting. Pays off every single day.

opts.name: Excavator (needs Geologist)
opts.why: Fun for completionists hunting minerals for the museum.

opts.name: Gemologist (needs Geologist)
opts.why: Late-game gems are worth a lot but you need most for gifting.

opts.name: Fisher
opts.why: Solid baseline income boost if you fish frequently.

opts.name: Trapper
opts.effect: Resources needed for crab pots reduced. Ore not required.
opts.why: Makes building a large crab pot network much cheaper.

opts.name: Angler (needs Fisher)
opts.why: With high-value fish like Legend (5,000g+) this is massive.

opts.name: Pirate (needs Fisher)
opts.effect: Chance to find treasure in fishing treasure chests doubled.
opts.why: Fun for getting rare items, but Angler makes more consistent gold.

opts.name: Mariner (needs Trapper)
opts.why: Transforms crab pots into pure profit with zero wasted bait.

opts.name: Luremaster (needs Trapper)
opts.why: Saves bait costs, but Mariner's no-junk perk is far more valuable.

opts.name: Forester
opts.why: Great early when you need tons of wood, less relevant later.

opts.name: Gatherer
opts.effect: Chance to get double forage items.
opts.why: Double forage = double income. Snowballs massively with Botanist at 10.

opts.name: Lumberjack (needs Forester)
opts.why: Hardwood is useful, but Mahogany Trees on Ginger Island are better.

opts.name: Tapper (needs Forester)
opts.why: Decent if you have 50+ tappers — niche but not the best pick.

opts.name: Botanist (needs Gatherer)
opts.effect: Foraged items are always Iridium quality.
opts.why: Absolute best. Every foraged item = maximum sell price, every time.

opts.name: Tracker (needs Gatherer)
opts.effect: Shows location of forageable items on the edges of screen.
opts.why: Useful for finding forage, but Botanist wins for raw income.

opts.name: Fighter
opts.effect: All attacks do 10% more damage. +15 max HP.
opts.why: Consistent damage boost in all combat situations, plus survivability.

opts.name: Scout
opts.why: Crit builds are inconsistent unless you also stack crit gear.

opts.name: Brute (needs Fighter)
opts.why: Good raw damage, but Defender's HP bonus keeps you alive longer.

opts.name: Defender (needs Fighter)
opts.why: 75 total extra HP means surviving harder hits in Skull Cavern.

opts.name: Acrobat (needs Scout)
opts.why: Situationally fun but overall weaker than Fighter path.

opts.name: Desperado (needs Scout)
opts.why: Glass cannon that requires crit stacking gear to shine.
